subject: What is wrong about this cpp file?

messages.author: 33ffbd5d5e9bca08
messages.subject: What is wrong about this cpp file?
parts:
hello all,

I wrote a cpp file similar as thetalog example, but nlminb constantly produces error as "Newton dropout because inner gradient had non-finite components. In addition: Warning message:
In nlminb(obj_dataset3$par, obj_dataset3$fn, obj_dataset3$gr) :NA/NaN function evaluation". 

I cannot picture anything wrong since the compiling of this cpp file works just fine. 

Here is my code if you do not mind to check my issue:

##############################################
##############################################

R code:
###generate data3
set.seed(123)
taudem<-0.01
sdbeta<-0.01

K<-35
eta<-0.5

meanp<-3.15
sigmap<-1.69

V<-c()
Y<-c()
###P is byth, I set it up arbitorally
P<-rep(0.5,100)
#P<--0.001*(seq(1,100,1)-50)^2+2.5
#pulse<-c(c(0,0),1,seq(0,96))

V[1]<-rlnorm(1,meanp,sigmap);
Y[1]<-rnorm(1,V[1],sqrt(taudem^2*V[1]))
trackP<-c()
trackPe<-c()
trackOe<-c()
#trackel<-c()
for(i in 1:99)
{
  e<-rnorm(1,0,sdbeta);
  if(e < (-V[i]*.95)) {e<- V[i]*.95};
  V[i+1]=V[i]+V[i]*(1-V[i]/K)*(1-eta*P[i])+V[i]*e;
  trackP<-c(trackP,(1-eta*P[i]));
  trackPe<-c(trackPe,V[i]*e);
  Ysigma=sqrt(taudem^2*V[i]);
  Y[i+1]=rnorm(1,V[i+1],Ysigma);
  trackOe<-c(trackOe,Ysigma);
}
data3<-list(Y=Y, P=P)

####setup initial values for parameters (here I use the true values that generate the data3 as initial values)
parameters_dataset3 <- list(
  X = c(7.789652,rep(0,(length(data3$Y)-1))),
  logK = log(35),
  logeta = log(0.5),
  logsdbeta = log(0.01),
  logtaudem = log(0.01)
)

####compile and find mle
obj_dataset3 <- MakeADFun(data3, parameters_dataset3, random="X", DLL="Daphnia_TMB_5_22_18",hessian=T)
newtonOption(obj_dataset3, smartsearch=FALSE)
opt_dataset3 <- nlminb(obj_dataset3$par, obj_dataset3$fn, obj_dataset3$gr)

cpp file:
#include <TMB.hpp>

template<class Type>
Type objective_function<Type>::operator() ()
{
  /* Data section */
  DATA_VECTOR(Y);
  DATA_VECTOR(P);
  /* Parameter section */
  PARAMETER_VECTOR(X);
  PARAMETER(logK);
  PARAMETER(logeta);
  PARAMETER(logsdbeta);
  PARAMETER(logtaudem);
  ADREPORT(X);
  ADREPORT(logK);
  ADREPORT(logeta);
  ADREPORT(logtaudem);
  /* Procedure section */
  Type eta=exp(logeta);
  Type sdbeta=exp(logsdbeta);
  Type K=exp(logK);
  Type taudem=exp(logtaudem);
  int timeSteps=Y.size();
  Type ans=0;
  for(int i=1;i<timeSteps;i++){
    Type m=X[i-1]*(1-X[i-1]/K)*(1-eta*P[i-1])+X[i-1];
  ans-=dnorm(X[i],m,X[i-1]*sdbeta,true);
  }
  for(int i=0;i<timeSteps;i++){
  Type R=taudem*taudem*X[i];
    ans-=dnorm(Y[i],X[i],sqrt(R),true);
  }
  return(ans);
}

messages.author: efdde7826c05851f
messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] What is wrong about this cpp file?
parts:
Dear Jing Jiao,

without looking at this with too much detail, I would reckon that this might have to do with the initial values for X. Initially X contains many zeroes. In the .cpp code, X then immediately affect the standard deviations in your calls to dnorm, leading to dnorm being evaluated at sd=0. This then seem to lead to NAs because dnorm divides by the sd (see https://kaskr.github.io/adcomp/dnorm_8hpp_source.html ). Hence, maybe the code will run better when you initialize the X-vector to different values than zeroes. (e.g. X= c(7.789652,rep(0.1,(length(data3$Y)-1))),). At least when I put these initial values in there instead, the code seems to be running.

Best regards,

Koen
